# Smoke scenario and certsuite-qe coverage

This inventory lists every test ID in `CATALOG.md` and compares two kinds of coverage:

- **certsuite-qe**: the `qe` flag passed to `AddCatalogEntry` in `tests/identifiers` (and `tests/preflight/catalog.go`), which marks tests that have a [certsuite-qe](https://github.com/redhat-best-practices-for-k8s/certsuite-qe) test. `certsuite generate qe-coverage-report` reads the same flag.
- **Smoke scenarios**: the dedicated entries in `scenarios.json`. Each one deploys workloads into an isolated namespace and asserts the expected claim state and a relevant object for each test it covers. Batch entries (`tests`) check several tests in one certsuite run.

The broader pre-main `--label-filter=all` smoke run is separate and does not count as dedicated scenario coverage.
Catalog IDs that cannot be exercised on the Kind smoke cluster say why; all other uncovered IDs are marked `No dedicated scenario` and are open gaps.

To add a scenario, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). For the multi-test batch scenarios, see [batches/README.md](batches/README.md).

## Scenarios

The 39 entries in `scenarios.json`, in run order. Each entry's lane says what it may run beside: entries in the same lane always run serially, and `--jobs` runs up to that many lanes at once. Only `namespaced` entries are safe to overlap freely; the other lanes touch cluster-wide state.

| Scenario | Lane | Manifest | Tests | What it deploys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TLS version range (non-compliant with Intermediate) | namespaced | `networking/tls-minimum-version/manifests/tls-noncompliant.yaml` | `networking-tls-minimum-version` | Deploys two nginx servers that each reject part of the Intermediate profile's required version range: one accepts only TLS 1.3 (rejecting TLS 1.2) and one accepts only TLS 1.2 (rejecting TLS 1.3). The Intermediate profile requires every version from TLS 1.2 through TLS 1.3, so both are non-compliant. One run covers both the below-minimum and the above-minimum version checks. |
| TLS version range (compliant with Intermediate profile) | namespaced | `networking/tls-minimum-version/manifests/tls-compliant.yaml` | `networking-tls-minimum-version` | Deploys one nginx server accepting both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 with only Intermediate-profile ciphers, and one plain HTTP server with no TLS configured. On non-OpenShift clusters the test defaults to the Intermediate profile (min TLS 1.2): the TLS server meets the version and cipher requirements, and the plain HTTP service is reported as informational rather than as a failure. |
| Unsecured container ports across nodes (plaintext + undeclared) | namespaced | `networking/unsecured-container-ports/manifests/plaintext-spread.yaml` | 2 | Deploys two plaintext HTTP workloads, two replicas each, with required hostname anti-affinity so every pair lands on different nodes. One declares its listening port, the other listens on 8080 without declaring it. One run covers both expectations: networking-unsecured-container-ports must fail every replica as plaintext (a single failure with the other pod unreachable is the cross-node openssl flake this guards against), and networking-undeclared-container-ports-usage must pass the declaring workload while failing the undeclared one. |
| Secured container ports across nodes (compliant) | namespaced | `networking/unsecured-container-ports/manifests/tls-spread.yaml` | `networking-unsecured-container-ports` | Deploys two TLS HTTP pods with required hostname anti-affinity so they land on different nodes. networking-unsecured-container-ports must pass, and both pods must be classified as using TLS. A pass with one pod marked unreachable is the cross-node openssl flake this scenario guards against. |
| Container checks (compliant) | namespaced | `manageability/container-checks/manifests/compliant.yaml` | 2 | Deploys two workloads that satisfy both container checks: one names its port http (an allowed port-name format) and one uses a tagged image. One run covers both checks, and the port-named workload keeps each check's compliant set non-empty so a silently skipped check cannot pass. |
| Container checks (non-compliant) | namespaced | `manageability/container-checks/manifests/violations.yaml` | 2 | Deploys two workloads that each violate one container check: one names its port sftp (outside the allowed port-name formats) and one uses an untagged image. One run covers both checks, with the violating workload named in each expectation so a foreign object appearing in the results cannot satisfy it. |
| Probes defined (compliant) | namespaced | `lifecycle/probes/manifests/golden.yaml` | 3 | Deploys a workload with TCP readiness, liveness and startup probes on nginx's listening port. One run covers all three probe checks. |
| Probes missing (non-compliant) | namespaced | `lifecycle/probes/manifests/violations.yaml` | 3 | Deploys three workloads, each identical to the compliant one except that it omits exactly one probe. One run covers all three probe checks, with each violating workload named in its own expectation so a missing check cannot be satisfied by another workload's result. |
| Default ingress and egress deny policy (compliant) | namespaced | `networking/network-policy-deny-all/manifests/deny-all.yaml` | `networking-network-policy-deny-all` | Deploys a NetworkPolicy with empty ingress and egress rules for the target pod. | Service mesh batch: workload without a sidecar (non-compliant) | cluster-scoped | `batches/service-mesh/manifests/violations.yaml` | `platform-alteration-service-mesh-usage` | The same installed mesh, but the target pod has no istio-proxy container. The check must fail that pod and name it. |
| Operators batch: golden OLM install (compliant) | operator | `batches/operators/golden/manifests/olm-golden.yaml` | 12 | A real OLM install from an in-cluster File-Based Catalog: an opm registry serves the catalog from a ConfigMap, the CatalogSource points at it by address, and OLM installs the bundle inline (CSV, CRD and a pause-image deployment) with no published bundle image. The operator carries a skipRange, a subscription, no clusterPermissions, one owned CRD with a structural schema, and its OperatorGroup targets a tenant namespace. Together these satisfy every check in the batch. operator-crd-openapi-schema has no failing scenario: apiextensions v1 requires structural schemas, so a served CRD without one cannot exist on any cluster. |
| Operators batch: one violation per object (non-compliant) | operator | `batches/operators/bad-csvs/manifests/bad-csvs.yaml` | 8 | Hand-written CSVs in a namespace with no OperatorGroup, so OLM marks them Failed without running any install strategy and their specs stay as written: one with an SCC clusterPermission, two sharing a base name and an owned CRD, and all without a subscription, skipRange or target namespaces. A CRD with a served version named v0 (valid for the apiserver, invalid for certsuite) covers crd-versioning. Each test must fail only on its own object. operator-semantic-versioning has no failing scenario here: OLM normalizes CSV spec.version through semver, so an invalid version cannot survive on the cluster. |
| Operators batch: unschedulable hugepages pod (non-compliant) | operator | `batches/operators/hugepages/manifests/hugepages.yaml` | `operator-pods-no-hugepages` | A real OLM install whose operator pod requests hugepages-2Mi. The Kind workers expose no hugepages, so the pod stays Pending while remaining attached to its CSV through the owner chain, and the hugepages check fails on it. The pod is deliberately left broken, so deploy waits for it to be unschedulable rather than running. |
| Operators batch: oversized catalog (non-compliant) | operator | `batches/operators/bundle-count/manifests/big-catalog.yaml` | `operator-catalogsource-bundle-count` | A real OLM install from a File-Based Catalog with 1002 bundles: one installable operator bundle plus 1001 filler bundles that exist only to push the catalog past the 1000-bundle limit. certsuite counts the bundles through the probe (grpcurl against the opm Service), so the needle distinguishes a real count from a probe failure. |
| Lifecycle batch: golden workloads (compliant) | node | `batches/lifecycle/manifests/golden.yaml` | 2 | A two-replica Deployment, so draining one node leaves the other replica schedulable, and a scalable CR (a CRD with a scale subresource but no status subresource) whose status a helper pod keeps equal to its spec. Pod recreation cordons and drains each node and the CR passes the scale check. |
| Lifecycle batch: pod with node assignment (non-compliant) | node | `batches/lifecycle/manifests/violations.yaml` | `lifecycle-pod-recreation` | The same two-replica Deployment with a nodeSelector that matches every Kind node, so the pods schedule normally. Pod recreation reports the node assignment instead of cordoning and draining, which is the check's failing branch. |
